_comment: All policy lives here. Gates contain logic only. Edit protected_paths for your repo (relative to this directory), keep read_only_verbs short, and add deny_patterns for commands that must never run from an agent. To reuse on another project: ./install.sh <repo>.

deny_patterns.reason: discarding every local change in one command; a ref in the middle (`git checkout HEAD -- .`) is the same command
piping a download straight into a shell
recursive delete of root, home or the working tree
docker system prune -a removes every image and volume
piping text into a shell runs whatever that text turns out to be
piping text into an interpreter runs whatever that text turns out to be
eval of a command substitution executes text that does not exist yet
xargs into a shell runs generated text
this git config key decides what git EXECUTES, so setting it is a way to run code later
git -c sets the same keys as git config, for one command, and those keys decide what git EXECUTES
the GIT_CONFIG_* variables are git config by another name, and this key decides what git executes

_alert_comment: Optional. A Slack or Discord incoming-webhook URL; every block is POSTed there. Leave empty to disable.
_interpreter_comment: Verbs whose arguments are executable payloads. Their quoted arguments are re-lexed and scanned for bare protected names, which is how `sh -c 'rm secrets'` is caught. Add any interpreter your team uses. Editors belong here too: vim -S, ex -c and sed -f all take a file of COMMANDS, which is a program by another name. And anything that runs a command LATER or on your behalf: at, batch, crontab, systemd-run, setsid, flock. `at -f work/go.sh` handed the file to a scheduler and nothing in the command line said what was in it.
_secret_comment: Paths whose CONTENT is the asset: .env, key files, a secrets/ directory. Every verb is denied on these, reads included, because the PocketOS agent did not delete a token, it READ one. protected_paths still allow cat/grep; secret_paths do not.
_self_protect_comment: Adds this guardrails directory and the project's .claude/settings*.json to the protected list at load time. Without it an agent can delete the guard that is supposed to stop it, which was true of this kit until it was attacked.
_read_only_comment: Verbs that can only look. Nothing that can execute belongs here: awk was on this list and on interpreter_verbs at the same time, so awk 'BEGIN{system("rm ...")}' walked straight through. The read-only list wins, so it must stay boring.
_execution_surface_comment: Files nobody runs on purpose and everybody runs anyway: a git hook fires on the next commit, a workflow on the next push, CLAUDE.md steers the agent itself. Writing to them is denied even though the canary is untouched, because the damage happens later and somewhere else. Reading stays allowed. Resolved against the project root, so an installed copy protects the repo's files, not the kit's. package.json and Makefile are deliberately NOT here: an agent adding a dependency edits package.json every day, so listing it would get the whole policy switched off. Add it yourself if your team's scripts are the thing you are protecting. Round nine added the ones a JavaScript or Python repo actually runs: .husky (git hooks installed by npm), .pre-commit-config.yaml, Taskfile/Justfile, .devcontainer, .vscode/settings.json. conftest.py, Makefile and package.json are deliberately NOT here, because a developer edits those daily; add them yourself if the agent has no business touching your test or build plumbing.
_recursive_readers_comment: Verbs that walk a whole tree. Pointed at a directory ABOVE a secret path they read it without ever naming it: `grep -r KEY .` and `tar -cf out.tar .` were both allowed until round six. An --exclude-dir / --exclude naming the secret re-allows them.
_exec_env_comment: Variables that decide what a command RUNS. Set in front of an ordinary command they are invisible: `PYTHONPATH=work python3 -c 'print(1)'` runs work/sitecustomize.py before the print. Their values are read as payloads: the file they name is scanned, and a directory is checked for the files an interpreter loads by itself. LD_PRELOAD and DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES are denied outright; an agent has no reason to set them inline.
_recursive_writers_comment: Verbs that change every file under a directory. Pointed at a parent of a guarded tree they never name it: `chmod -R 000 .` leaves the protected files unusable and the command mentions nothing but a dot.
_home_execution_surface_comment: The same idea as execution_surface, outside the repository. Writing ~/.claude/settings.json injects env into every future agent shell, ~/.zshrc runs on the next terminal, ~/.gitconfig can set core.hooksPath for every repo on the machine, and ~/.ssh/config can set a ProxyCommand. Reading them stays allowed. Set protect_home_surface to false to switch this off.
